newsitem.title: USA: Georgian diplomat to face trial in fatal car crash.
newsitem.headline: Georgian diplomat to face trial in fatal car crash.

text.p: Lawyers for Georgian diplomat Gueorgui Makharadze, who faces a July trial, said Tuesday they entered a plea of innocent to charges involving a car crash that killed a teenage girl two months ago.

After a brief court hearing in which the judge set a July 21 trial date, defence attorneys told reporters they entered the innocent plea on behalf of Makharadze, the second highest- ranking official at the Georgian Embassy.

Makharadze, who was stripped of diplomatic immunity by his own government, allegedly was drinking and speeding on the night of the Jan. 4 accident that killed a 16-year-old Brazilian girl who was living in a Maryland suburb.
Makharadze faces charges of involuntary manslaughter for the death of Joviane Waltrick and four counts of aggravated assault for injuries to others in the five-car crash.

Makharadze has been charged with running into a vehicle waiting at a stop light in downtown Washington. The force of the crash catapulted the second vehicle into a third car, killing Waltrick, who was a passenger.
Defence attorney E. Lawrence Barcella during the hearing sought a jury trial and asked that Makharadze continue to remain free in the custody of the Georgian Embassy, a request granted by the judge.
Washington, D.C., Superior Court Judge Harold Cushenberry set the next status hearing in the case for April 11 to consider the dates for the filing of various motions.
Makharadze, 35, who had been a rising star in the Georgian foreign service, did not speak during the arraignment.
After the hearing, Waltrick's mother, Viviani Wagner, said Makharadze had not attempted to personally contact her about the accident.
"Justice is just starting to be made," she said, speaking through an interpreter. She said she attended the hearing to see for herself what happens in the case.
